ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are three cards facing up, and the visible numbers from left to right are 44, 59, and 38 respectively. The problem states that the sum of the numbers on the two sides of each card is the same, and that the numbers on the hidden sides of the three cards are all prime numbers. Then reason: Let the common sum of the numbers on the two sides of each card be S, then the prime numbers on the three hidden sides are S-44, S-59, and S-38 respectively. Because S-59 is a positive prime number, S>59. If S is an even number, then S-44 and S-38 are both even numbers greater than 2, and cannot be prime numbers, so S cannot be an even number; S must be an odd number. Thus S-59 is an even number; it is also a prime number, so it can only equal 2. Therefore S-59=2, obtaining S=61. The three prime numbers on the hidden sides are 61-44=17, 61-59=2, and 61-38=23. Their average is (17+2+23)/3=42/3=14.

Barry wrote 6 different numbers, one on each side of 3 cards, and laid the cards on a table, as shown. The sums of the two numbers on each of the three cards are equal. The three numbers on the hidden sides are prime numbers. What is the average of the hidden prime numbers?

<image1>

method.method_draft: First read the image: the three visible card faces show 44, 59, and 38. From the text, assign a common total S to each card, so the hidden primes are S-44, S-59, and S-38. Since the hidden number behind 59 is prime and positive, S>59. If S were even, then S-44 and S-38 would both be even and greater than 2, so they could not be prime. Therefore S is odd. Then S-59 is an even prime, so it must be 2. Thus S=61, giving hidden primes 17, 2, and 23; their average is (17+2+23)/3=14.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the face-up numbers are two even numbers, 44 and 38, and one odd number, 59. Let p be the hidden prime on the back of the 59 card. Then the common card sum is 59+p. If p were an odd prime, then 59+p would be even. Subtracting the even visible numbers 44 and 38 from this even common sum would make the other two hidden values even; because the common sum is greater than 59, these even hidden values would exceed 2, impossible for primes. Hence p must be the only even prime, p=2. So the common sum is 61, and the other hidden primes are 61-44=17 and 61-38=23. The average is (2+17+23)/3=14.

Image description: The attached image shows three upright rectangular cards on a table. The visible face-up numbers from left to right are 44, 59, and 38. The visible numbers 44 and 38 are even, while 59 is odd.

Reasoning: Let p be the hidden prime on the back of the card showing 59. Since the sum of the two numbers on each card is the same, the common sum is 59 + p. If p were an odd prime, then 59 + p would be even. Then the hidden numbers behind 44 and 38 would be (59 + p) - 44 and (59 + p) - 38, both even. Also, because p would be at least 3, the common sum would be at least 62, making those hidden even numbers greater than 2. But the only even prime is 2, so this is impossible. Therefore p must be the only even prime, p = 2. The common sum is then 59 + 2 = 61. The other hidden primes are 61 - 44 = 17 and 61 - 38 = 23. Their average is (2 + 17 + 23) / 3 = 42 / 3 = 14.
